business_patterns.top_pattern: OH DSNP acute hospital spend is concentrated in two hospitals
business_patterns.pattern_details: OH DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased materially and is concentrated in two hospitals rather than spread broadly across the market. Both claim volume and paid per admit moved up, which points to a combined provider mix and reimbursement issue rather than utilization alone. The increase is overwhelmingly tied to KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON and GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the single largest operational pattern and creates a direct contracting, provider mix, and UM action opportunity in OH.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Pull claim-level episodes for KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON and GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL, validate the admission mix, and run a joint network and UM review of reimbursement terms, level of care, and avoidable acute utilization for DSNP HMO.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is heavily concentrated in two hospitals and flagged as low baseline and low volume, so claim-level confirmation should precede contract or UM escalation.
evidence_summary: OH DSNP HMO acute hospital spend rose about $1.3M.
KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON added about $0.7M on 662 more claims, with paid per admit up about $1.1K.
GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL added about $0.6M on 438 more claims, with paid per admit up about $1.3K.
The increase is concentrated almost entirely in those two hospitals; the named vascular procedure contributed only about $13.6K.

This looks like provider concentration plus high-cost case emergence inside one acute facility.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single hospital is driving most of the CA DSNP acute increase, making this a focused network and UM intervention point.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review EL CAMINO acute admissions and contract performance together, with special focus on trauma-related stays, outlier payment behavior, and whether those cases were managed at the intended level of care for DSNP HMO.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The signal is concentrated in one hospital and includes low-baseline high-cost cases, so the underlying claims should be confirmed before broader network action.

business_patterns.pattern_details: CA IP Med/Surg cost growth is being driven by a small number of very high-cost inpatient admissions rather than a broad case-mix shift. Most of the dollars sit in trauma-related surgical stays, with an additional sepsis signal at EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL. This is a rare catastrophic outlier pattern that needs case-level review, not a broad policy change.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of admissions can materially move spend and may represent transplant-like or catastrophic management opportunities for clinical and UM teams.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send the identified CA inpatient cases for case-level clinical and UM review to confirm severity, level of care, and any outlier payment drivers before considering reimbursement or policy changes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by a handful of one- and two-case catastrophic admissions.
evidence_summary: CA IP Med/Surg rare cases added about $0.9M.
Five trauma-related diagnoses contributed about $0.9M total, with single cases ranging from about $90.5K to $254.0K.
The largest cases were S52551B at about $254.0K, S82251C at about $222.2K, and S32592A at about $206.0K.
Separate sepsis admissions added about $41.7K across 2 claims at EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Not Mapped transport claims are creating a validation gate
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH / VA / TX / Not Mapped transport and outpatient misc
business_patterns.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the increase is sitting in Not Mapped buckets tied largely to transportation providers, which creates a validation gate before interpreting this as pure utilization growth. The strongest signal is MIDWEST MEDICAL TRANSPORT COMPANY in OH and VA, with additional OH outpatient misc transport and a smaller TX signal from KON VENTURES. This pattern may reflect true transport use growth, but mapping and classification leakage need to be ruled out first.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If these claims are misclassified, the organization could misread authorization, site-of-service, and utilization trends and take the wrong action.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate facility mapping, service classification, and authorization status for transport claims from MIDWEST MEDICAL TRANSPORT COMPANY and KON VENTURES, then separate confirmed ambulance utilization growth from classification leakage before UM or reimbursement changes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Multiple groups carry Not Mapped and unmapped flags, so classification and authorization assignment must be confirmed before interpreting utilization or provider performance.
evidence_summary: OH Medicare HMO Not Mapped transport added about $179.8K on 885 more claims at MIDWEST MEDICAL TRANSPORT COMPANY.
OH DSNP HMO Not Mapped transport added about $164.3K on 550 more claims at the same provider.
VA DSNP HMO Not Mapped transport added about $131.1K on 391 more claims.
OH outpatient misc transport added about $75.4K on about 260 claims, and TX KON VENTURES added about $16.5K on 68 claims.

business_patterns.pattern_details: IN and OH show a concentrated inpatient outlier pattern rather than broad utilization growth. The largest driver is one very high-cost Medicare HMO trauma admission in IN, with additional one-case Med/Surg stays in IN and OH tied to infectious, digestive, vascular, and sepsis-related admissions. This is best treated as a rare acute admission pattern requiring case review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A few inpatient admissions are materially affecting spend and may point to care management or outlier reimbursement opportunities.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route the identified IN and OH admissions to clinical and UM teams for case-level review, including severity, LOS, transfer pathway, and any outlier reimbursement terms on the trauma and sepsis-related stays.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most of the increase comes from one-case or two-case admissions, including one very large trauma case.
evidence_summary: IN Medicare HMO acute hospital spend added about $267.9K, led by one trauma admission worth about $254.0K.
IN and OH IP Med/Surg rare cases added about $135.1K, led by GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL cases for A4101 at about $35.9K and A0472 at about $30.4K.
A separate OH sepsis-with-MCC case added about $31.2K.
Most of the signal comes from isolated admissions rather than a repeatable broad trend.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Outpatient chemotherapy episodes are landing in Not Mapped buckets
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH / CA / TX / OP IV Thrpy/Oncology and OP Mgmt Oth Misc

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL

business_patterns.pattern_details: Outpatient chemotherapy-related episodes are repeatedly showing up in Not Mapped buckets across OH and CA, with a smaller related outpatient misc signal spanning CA and TX. The pattern is concentrated at GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL, KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON, and EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL and appears tied to chemotherapy drug claims rather than a broad outpatient shift. This is a distinct authorization and mapping issue because oncology drug episodes may be classified outside the expected service line.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Misclassified chemotherapy activity can distort oncology trend reporting, obscure authorization performance, and hide site-of-care opportunities.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate chemotherapy authorization records, drug coding, and service-line assignment for Z5111, Z5112, C180, and C679 episodes, and confirm whether these claims should be grouped under oncology rather than Not Mapped outpatient buckets.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Repeated oncology-related claims are landing in Not Mapped buckets, so service-line classification and authorization mapping may be distorting the pattern.
evidence_summary: OH outpatient oncology added about $118.0K at GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL on 21 chemotherapy drug claims under Z5111.
OH outpatient misc chemotherapy added about $136.3K at KETTERING HEALTH DAYTON and GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL under Z5112 and Z5111.
CA chemotherapy-related episodes added about $105.8K, led by EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL under C679 and C180.
Across these groups, chemotherapy is the dominant signal; smaller transport tails were only about $25.5K in OH and $13.0K in CA / TX.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TX IP Med/Surg has a small number of very high-cost outliers
business_patterns.pattern_details: TX IP Med/Surg growth is being driven by only a few very expensive admissions, not a widespread utilization trend. One esophageal case is the clear outlier, with several smaller high-cost cases in skin and digestive-related diagnoses behind it. The right response is targeted case review rather than broad policy or network changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A very small number of claims is responsible for the TX increase, so targeted intervention can be more effective than broad utilization controls.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review the identified TX inpatient cases for severity, level of care, and any outlier reimbursement mechanics, starting with the Q398 esophageal admission.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Only four claims drive the full increase, including one case worth about $173.5K.
evidence_summary: TX IP Med/Surg rare cases added about $231.6K on 4 claims.
The largest case was Q398 under Major Esophageal Disorders with MCC at about $173.5K.
C439, L100, and K2101 added another roughly $58.0K across 3 claims.
Paid per admit was very high across the identified cases, confirming an outlier pattern.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Other scattered low-volume acute and post-acute cases are emerging
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NJ / TX / WI / CA / OH / IN / Acute Hospital and SNF - FREE STANDING
key_driver_codes: Other O.R. Procedures for Multiple Significant Trauma with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Outside the main hotspots, the remaining increase is fragmented across several states, products, and settings and is mostly driven by isolated acute or post-acute cases. The largest residual piece is a DSNP acute hospital cluster across NJ / TX / WI, but even that is led by a few single-case TX admissions. Small Medicare HMO acute and IN SNF/NF signals are present, but they are too sparse to support broad action on their own.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: These residual signals can distract from bigger action areas unless they are first confirmed as real and repeatable.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate the scattered low-volume cases at claim level before changing policy or contracts; if confirmed, send the TX acute cases to UM/reimbursement review and the IN SNF/NF case to post-acute clinical review.
business_patterns.validation_reason: These groups are fragmented and mostly single-case or very small-run events, with repeated low-baseline and small-n flags.
evidence_summary: NJ / TX / WI DSNP HMO acute hospital spend added about $446.7K, led by two single TX admissions worth about $173.5K and $222.2K.
CA / OH Medicare HMO acute hospital added about $56.4K across 3 claims.
IN DSNP HMO SNF and IN NF each added about $9.2K on a single connective tissue or rheumatoid arthritis case.
All included groups carry low-baseline or small-n flags, which limits immediate enterprise action.

executive_summary.headline: The biggest cost story is concentrated DSNP acute hospital pressure in OH and CA, with separate validation gates in Not Mapped transport and outpatient chemotherapy and a smaller set of rare inpatient outliers.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: The largest actionable dollars sit in provider-concentrated DSNP acute hospital spend, especially in OH and CA, where both claim volume and paid per admit moved up. A second major theme is validation: Not Mapped transport and outpatient chemotherapy claims may be obscuring true authorization, service-line, and provider-mix trends. The remaining clinical impact is driven by rare catastrophic inpatient cases in CA, TX, IN, and OH and should be handled through case-level review rather than broad policy changes.
recommended_focus_order: OH DSNP HMO acute hospital provider concentration
CA DSNP HMO acute pressure plus CA rare inpatient outliers
Not Mapped transport and outpatient chemotherapy validation
